pr_title: Support for store parameter in geo_shape field
pr_body:
This PR adds support for storing geo_shape fields as a lucene stored field. The geometry will be stored normalised in Well known binary format (WKB).

Reading geometries from WKB is generally much faster than parsing geometries in WKT or GeoJson in source, therefore we changed the ValueFetcher method to read geometries from the store values whenever are present. This should speed up the fields API. 

In particular we are suing this API in vector tiles so it should speed up this API too. The user has the choice of using more disk space in order to speed up generating vector tiles.

In our test data we saw an increase of ~20% on index size:

```
green  open shapes          Lel6q7CXTfS4xXjl7EB_XA 1 0 13165248 0 6.7gb 6.7gb
green  open shapes_stored   GNko7pi7QQqfx4mexa1YMQ 1 0 13165248 0   9gb   9gb
```

And a ~25% speed up when generating vector tiles:

issue_context.title: Use geo_shape stored field to speed up fetching geometries through fields API
issue_context.body:
### Description

Currently the fields API fetches the geometries from source. That means we need to navigate the _source and then parsing the geometry either from GeoJson or WKT. This has been prove slow for big geometries, we suspect because parsing thousand of points from test to doubles is expensive.

We did a micro benchmark and it seems is almost equal expense to pare WKT or GeoJson:

```
Benchmark                               Mode  Cnt    Score   Error   Units
ParseGeometryBenchmark.parseGeoJson    thrpt   20    1,547 ± 0,009  ops/ms
ParseGeometryBenchmark.parseWKT        thrpt   20    1,414 ± 0,010  ops/ms
```

Elasticsearch will store _source in the encoding the document is sent and it supports SMILE. SMILE is a binary format based on Json so it stores numerical data with its binary representation so it should provide us with a speed-up:

```
Benchmark                               Mode  Cnt    Score   Error   Units
ParseGeometryBenchmark.parseSmile      thrpt   20   11,928 ± 0,086  ops/ms
```

So this provide us already with a nice boost. Finally, [WKB](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/82706) is the binary equivalent to WKT, so we microbenchmark it as well:

```
Benchmark                               Mode  Cnt    Score   Error   Units
ParseGeometryBenchmark.parseWKB        thrpt   20  236,367 ± 4,844  ops/ms
```

Thats quite a big boost. 

Therefore what we propose in this issue is to enable the possibility of store geo_shape fields which is currently disabled. The format to be added will  be in WKB and then teach the fields API to read from that field if exists. That should provide a nice speed up. One debatable thing if this should be an opt-in or an opt-out as the downside is that we are storing another copy of the geometry, hence the index size becomes bigger.

Why we want to do this?

Vector Tile search uses the fields API to read geometries from the data nodes and add them to the final vector tile. It actually retrieves geometries by size so you end up always with the biggest geometries on the result of a query. This has shown that one of the bottle necks we have in performance is parsing this geometries.

trade-off

We are trading fetching speed for size of the index. A quick check in some test data provides the following results:

```
green open shapes_geojson    L98JtffsQaycFsRMNWqbtg 1 0 13165241 0 6.7gb 6.7gb
green open shapes_smile      pFjzoHhUTE6r6nxHW5AkUA 1 0 13165241 0 7.2gb 7.2gb
green open shapes_stored    fXUCORabTUaz4fkpD7do8w 1 0 13165241 0 8.8gb 8.8gb
```

That is a 7% increase for smile and a 30% for the new stored value in WKB format.
comments: It's interesting that SMILE yields a 7% larger index, most likely because it writes doubles using 8 bytes that are hardly compressible, when the text representation is often more compact.

I'd be interested in getting a sense of how these microbenchmarks translate into macrobenchmarks, ie. how long does it take to fetch vector tiles dependeng on whether data is stored in JSON, SMILE or WKB?

```

review_comments: I notice we have no error checking here, but perhaps this is not a situation that could ever occur. If we had simply done a cast, we would at least get a class cast exception. This code silently ignores those cases.
I added a an else statement that throws an error
It is broken into two polygons, we store the normalised version of the polygon.
Yes, I understand, the same misunderstanding I made above about it being clockwise.
Wow! Quite a lot of mocking just to test the `valueFetcher` method. But I guess this was unavoidable.
yep, it is required if we want to mock it,

Should there be more tests in this class? Seems like we have added the most import capabilities to GeoShapeWithDocValuesFieldMapper, so I kind-of expected this test class to test more. Perhaps it is not needed because we have more tests elsewhere?
Yes, and actually this test was wrong. I fixed it and added more tests.
Nice expansion on the range of tests
So I guess the user has no control over whether to pull the stored value or doc values. I assume this is because the stored value is much faster. Are there any negatives to this choice?
The control is wether the user chooses to store the geo_shape or not (default).
I thought ES handled clockwise only for short edges, but perhaps not?
This polygon is clockwise and ES expects counterclockwise by default, therefore it splits the polygon across the dateline.
Ah, yes, that makes more sense!
